alternatives.label: Human health, disease and behaviour
alternatives.concept: Study the scientific basis of human health and disease through anatomy, physiology, molecular pathology, pharmacology, infection, neuroscience, psychology and health research. This is a sustained medical-science response to Medicine’s disease-mechanism and evidence strands. It does not provide the programme’s clinical reasoning and examination sequence, assessed patient care, acute medical skills or physician qualification.
progression: Foundations of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior precede their formally dependent specialist courses. Introductory disease, neuroscience and social psychology appear before later related 300-level work where available; all prerequisites and planned semester offerings pass.

candidates.label: Supervised clinical medicine and patient care
candidates.reason: A distinct clinically oriented second alternative would require sustained supervised patient care, physical examination and clinical diagnosis. UCR teaches relevant anatomy, disease science, health psychology and ethical reasoning but has no medical practice or patient-contact courses to form a defensible 24-course clinical pathway. These components remain substantive gaps, not cosmetic substitutions.

candidates.label: Research on disease from molecules to populations
candidates.reason: The first UCR programme already gives this direction its substantive curriculum through molecular biology, organ-level disease, neuroscience, epidemiology, laboratory methods and systematic evidence synthesis; a separate title would duplicate its main organising logic.

selection.assessment: The 24-course programme is a strong UCR academic response to disease mechanisms, public health, cognition and patient experience, with clinically specific training explicitly absent. A second medical-practice route cannot be supported by UCR patient contact, examination or clinical reasoning courses; research from molecules to populations is already a core emphasis of the first programme.

notes.text: UCR offers substantial study of disease mechanisms and health evidence. It does not reproduce Medicine’s assessed clinical reasoning, physical examination, patient encounters or professional medical formation. This comparison does not establish admission to a medical master or a qualification to practise medicine.

audience.programmeDescription: Medicine connects the mechanisms of health and disease with clinical reasoning, physical examination, patient contact, research and medical professional development. This comparison follows the regular 2024 entrant cohort through its three documented years.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This UCR programme provides sustained scientific study of human health and disease, with anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, infection, neuroscience and health research. These subjects respond directly to Medicine’s scientific foundations. Clinical reasoning levels, physical examination, acute medical skills, assessed patient care and medical professional formation remain substantial gaps; psychology and biomedical laboratory courses do not replace them.

curriculum.limitation: The documented cohort comprises 60,56 and64 EC across its three years. Clinical and research minor topics depend on the permitted selection. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 42 EC. RADAr participation is an additional 0-EC requirement; passing it is not required.
